questions.q: Who controls when a Tool gets used, versus a Resource, versus a Prompt?
options: All three are always controlled by the user
Tools: the model. Resources: the application. Prompts: the user
Tools: the server administrator. Resources: the model. Prompts: the application
There is no difference in who controls each one
questions.explain: This three-way split is the core distinction: the model decides when to call a tool, the application decides when to pull in a resource for context, and the user explicitly invokes a prompt template.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a Resource, not a Tool?
options: Sending a message to a team channel
Creating a calendar event
A file's contents exposed read-only for context, such as file:///path/to/document.md
Searching for and booking a flight
questions.explain: Resources are passive, read-only data for context (file contents, database schemas). Sending messages, creating events, and booking flights are all actions a model would call as tools.

questions.q: What is the difference between a direct resource and a resource template?
options: A direct resource has a fixed URI pointing at specific data; a resource template uses a parameterized URI for flexible queries, like travel://activities/{city}/{category}
A direct resource can only be text; a resource template can only be images
There is no real difference between them
A resource template is only used for tools, never resources
questions.explain: A direct resource like calendar://events/2024 points at one specific thing. A resource template like travel://activities/{city}/{category} is a pattern that can be filled in dynamically, e.g. travel://activities/barcelona/museums.

questions.q: What protocol operation does a client use to discover which tools a server offers?
options: tools/call
resources/read
tools/list
prompts/invoke
questions.explain: tools/list returns the array of available tool definitions with their schemas. tools/call is used afterward to actually execute one of those tools.

questions.q: The searchFlights example tool definition in this lesson uses which fields, matching the format from the tool-schema lesson earlier in this course?
options: name, description, and inputSchema (a JSON Schema object)
Only a raw SQL query string
A single free-text paragraph with no structure
name and a list of other tools it depends on
questions.explain: The searchFlights example has name, description, and inputSchema defining origin, destination, and date as typed, required properties — the same name/description/schema shape taught in Chapter 2.
